To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) abductive explanations can be computed by bottom-up model generation, (2) this computation is done by a transformation to disjunctive logic programs, and (3) the transformation can be done in polynomial time.

(1) the stable models of an arbitrary program can be characterized as the xpoints of a disjuntive program obtained by an appropriate transformation of the original program; and (2) the xpoints of an arbitrary disjunctive logic program can be computed in parallel bottomup by a fixpoint iteration.

abductive logic programs can be transformed to disjunctive logic programs in a way such that the stable models of the latter program correspond exactly to the generalized stable models (explanations) of the original program.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new xpoint-based semantics for abductive programs.

the development of a uniform and general framework for computing abductive logic program explanations, which are useful for many applications such as model-based diagnosis, belief revision, and nonmonotonic reasoning.
the development of a new semantics for abductive programs that can be implemented by a model generation procedure for arbitrary logic programs with integrity constraints and abducibles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed xpoint semantics for the transformation of abductive logic programs to disjunctive logic programs provides a general framework to deal with abductive logic programs, and the proposed bottom-up model generation procedure for the transformed programs provides an efficient and effective way to compute abductive explanations from a wide class of abductive programs.

our new xpoint-based semantics for abductive programs, which has the advantage of having a bottom-up procedure, is more general than the previous ones in the sense that it covers all the previous ones as special cases and it is more flexible in the sense that we have a wider choice of abducibles.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the abductive explanations of an abductive logic program P can be computed by the stable model semantics of the disjunctive logic program T(P), which is obtained from P by a simple program transformation.
abductive reasoning can be viewed as an extension of the well-known stable model semantics.

the xpoint semantics is a generalization of the answer set semantics for disjunctive logic programs, and the transformation provides a uniform framework for computing abductive answers for general logic programs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the abducibles in an abductive logic program can be viewed as the atoms of a disjuctive logic program, which is obtained by transforming the original abductive logic program.
the abductive semantics of logic programs can be captured as a disjunctivization process, and the abductive semantics is not restricted to a special class of programs.
the transformation can be applied in the presence of both negative and positive hypotheses.
